item.title: Constraints on interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in light of DESI DR2: The role of the interaction term
item.description: arXiv:2610.30784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analyses suggest a preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state (EoS) that crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Interactions between dark energy and dark matter can also produce an apparent phantom-divide crossing in the effective dark energy EoS. item.title: The telescope that could reveal what dark matter and dark energy are
item.description: The Roman telescope is NASA’s newest space observatory. Every 10 months, it will get the equivalent of about 1000 years' worth of Hubble observations. Will it find the answers to our questions about dark matter and dark energy?

item.title: Sound-Horizon-Agnostic Forecast for Constraints on H_0 and Sigma m_nu from BAO, CMB Lensing, Supernovae and LSST-like Galaxy Lensing

item.description: arXiv:2610.30265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ionizing radiation that galaxies release into their surroundings depends on whether efficient Lyman continuum (LyC) escape coincides with strong photon production. item.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
item.description: Image: This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
